toolchain._doc: Left blank on purpose. `gd setup` fills these in on the machine config, not here. A path committed here is a path that is wrong for everyone who is not the author.

godot.notes: `console` is what every agent-driven invocation uses: on Windows the plain .exe detaches from the terminal and the caller receives no stdout, which reads as a hang. `source_root` is optional - when blank, `gddoc index` has the engine generate its own class reference with --doctool.

models._doc: Starting model per agent, and the escalation ladder `gd run` climbs when a job keeps failing its gate. Route on capability, not on headline per-token price: on a long build, cached-input reads dominate the bill, so a stronger model with cheaper cache reads can finish a phase for less than a weaker one. Reserve the top tier for work where the quality gap is visible to the player.

gd-planner.why: decomposition and judgement; every job downstream inherits its mistakes, and it runs once per phase so the cost is small

gd-art-director.why: palette and lighting contracts are taste, and taste is where models differ most visibly

gd-critic.why: pure visual judgement; a weak critic silently lowers the ceiling of every gauntlet round it accepts

gd-modeler.why: asset work is an aesthetic task disguised as a scripting task

gd-mechanics.why: engine systems, physics, shaders - correctness-critical and the highest-volume role, so not the place for the priciest tier

gd-rigger.why: precise iterative math across many attempts

gd-perf.why: diagnosis; a wrong bisection wastes the whole session, but the triage order is already written down

gd-playtester.why: mechanical - write the plan, run it, report the numbers. No judgement required, and it runs constantly

gd-researcher.why: volume reading, summary out, and every claim is checked against the local API index anyway

gd-scribe.why: documentation and learnings extraction - reads a lot, writes prose, no engine judgement

models._haiku_note: Nothing defaults to haiku. It sits on the ladder as a floor for future cheap roles; no current agent's job is mechanical enough to justify it, and a wrong answer from a gate-facing agent costs more than the tier saves.
models._host_doc: Which assistant front-end this install is driven from: 'claude', 'codex', or 'auto' to detect from the environment. GD_HOST overrides it per shell. The ladder and the per-agent model above are Claude's; a host entry below replaces both when that host is active. Everything else in this file - budget, playtest defaults, the snap grid - is host-neutral, because it describes the game and the engine, not the thing driving them.

claude._doc: Claude Code. Agents are files under .claude/agents/ whose `model:` frontmatter must agree with the table above; `gd models` checks that. Inherits `ladder` and `agents` from the parent block - they are not repeated here, so there is exactly one place to change a Claude routing decision.

codex._doc: Codex CLI. Codex has no per-agent model surface - agents are skills, and a skill cannot pin a model - so the routing below is what `gd run` dispatches with (`codex exec -m <model>`), and there is no frontmatter for `gd models` to drift against. The roles and their reasons are the same as Claude's; only the tier names differ.
codex._ladder_why: Four rungs, mapped to the same shape as the Claude ladder: a cheap floor for mechanical roles, two middle tiers, and the most capable model reserved for the work where the quality gap is visible to the player. gpt-5.5 is deliberately absent - a previous-generation model on a gate-facing role costs more in re-runs than the tier saves.
codex._agents_note: Bare strings, not {model, why} objects: the *reason* a role sits where it does is host-neutral and lives once in `models.agents` above. Only the model name differs per host. The three engine roles start at `terra` rather than `sol` because they have two rungs of headroom above them and are the highest-volume roles on the board; `gd run` escalates them if a gate keeps failing. First-pass mapping - tune it against real escalation counts, and record the reason here when you do.

_doc: SHIPPED DEFAULTS. Identical on every machine, and overwritten by every upgrade - so nothing machine-specific and nothing game-specific may live here. Toolchain paths are discovered by `gd setup` and written to ~/.claude/gatekeeper.machine.json; per-game numbers go in that game's <project>/.planning/config.json. `gd config` prints all three layers and which one each value came from.
